sentences.text: The hind limbs of Faxinalipterus are relatively long and better preserved than the front limbs.

Original describers considered Faxinalipterus perhaps the oldest known pterosaur, possibly predating European finds from the Norian, though a 2022 study later reinterpreted the fossils as belonging to the clade Lagerpetidae, a group of pterosauromorphs.
The species Faxinalipterus minimus was named and described in 2010 by José Fernando Bonaparte, Marina Bento Soares, and César Leandro Schultz.
Fossils were found in 2002 and 2005 at a site 1.5 kilometers northeast of Faxinal do Soturno in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from the Caturrita Formation dating to 220–215 million years ago.
An upper jaw fragment with three teeth was initially referred to Faxinalipterus but was later determined to belong to a distinct species named Maehary.
Original describers concluded Faxinalipterus was the most basal known pterosaur, citing features like a lack of tibia-fibula fusion, a thin radius, and an unfused coracoid.
Because the Caturrita Formation consists of terrestrial sandstones, the original describers suggested Faxinalipterus evolved in a terrestrial habitat rather than a coastal one.
A 2022 study reinterpreted the fossils as belonging to the clade Lagerpetidae, a group of pterosauromorphs.

Alexander Kellner suggested Faxinalipterus might be a basal pterosauromorph or a sister taxon to Ornithodira rather than a pterosaur, while Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia (2013) stated he could not find unequivocal pterosaur features in the fossils and noted the purported humerus is unlike those of Triassic pterosaurs.
